newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Aug 18.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Aug 18.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Monday:
* Apprehension over the fate of currencies in the region with the Dow's slump of over 200 points, its steepest fall in 10-years, will likely weigh down the market, traders said.

* "We continue to advise caution in investing in the equities market and wait for further developments that would provide a clearer direction of the financial markets," said BPI Securities Corp in its weekly outlook.
* Sun Hung Kai Securities said that if the main index breaches 2,550, the next support may be at 2,430 points.
* On Friday, the Philippine composite index fell 44.56 points closing lower for the seventh straight session at a 21-month low of 2,448.93 points.
* The Dow Jones on Friday slumped 247.37 points, the steepest point fall since October 1987, at 7,694.66. PLDT's ADR closed lower by $0/12 at $29/05.
* The Philippine peso ended lower at 29.80 to a U.S. dollar versus 29.48.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average dropped to 14.0625 percent from 14.09375 percent.
* The Philippines posted a 5.706 billion peso budgetary surplus in the first seven months of the year, up from 4.9 billion registered a year ago, data from the Bureau of Treasury showed.
* The Philippine government's total debt stock stood at 1.148 trillion pesos as of June 30, data released by the Department of Finance stated.
* JG Summit Holdings Inc said its net income fell to 1.63 billion pesos for the first half of the year from 3.39 billion the same period last year.
* Benpres Holdings Corp's net income for the first six months of the year reached 1.08 billion pesos from 978 million a year ago.
* Alsons Consolidated Resources Inc said its net income for the first half of the year fell sharply to 299.47 million pesos from 567.29 a year ago.
* C&P Homes Inc posted a net income of 1.53 billion pesos the first half of the year from 1.37 billion the same period last year.
* The country's largest shipping firm, William Gothong & Aboitiz said it posted a 181.31 million peso net income for the six months to June 30 from 217.50 million last year.
* Filinvest Development Corp said its first half net income was lower at 1.30 billion pesos from 1.84 billion a year ago.
* Atlas Fertilizer Corp said it made 13.6 million pesos for the second quarter of its fiscal year ending June from a 28.4 million loss last year.

* Kepphil Philippines Holdings Inc said it generated a net profit of 48.32 million pesos for the first two quarters of the year from 57.84 million a year ago. For the first half of this year, Kepphil Shipyard Inc made 33.05 million in earnings from 48.8 million in the same period in 1996.
* Cebu Shipyard and Engineering Works Inc said its first half proft was almost flat at 28.17 million pesos from the year-ago level 27.77 million.
* The Bankers Association of the Philippines said it will establish a sophisticated credit report system to minimise risks in consumer loams.

* Newspaper BusinessWorld said quoting central bank managing director Amando Tetangco that the bank plans to stay out of the foreign exchange market this week even as the peso is expected to soon breach the 30 pesos to one dollar mark, the lowest ever for the embattled currency.
